items.excerpt: China's free web-novel platforms are aggressively purging AI-generated fiction — Fanqie Novel rejected 100,000+ low-quality titles in June alone — but AI detectors are so imperfect that human authors now anxiously self-edit to avoid 'writing like an AI.' The piece frames the paradox of AI screening reshaping the web-novel writing craft.

items.excerpt: At the 35th IPA Congress in Kuala Lumpur, three sessions on children's publishing argued that format and quality of content — not AI itself — shape how digital-native kids read, and pressed publishers on closing a widening global literacy gap.

items.excerpt: Two dueling surveys on AI audiobook narration: a Spoken-commissioned study found 61% of listeners mistook AI voices for human and favored them in multi-character scenes, while an Audio Publishers Association study shows willingness to try AI narration fell from 70% (2025) to 61% (2026) — human narration still preferred.

items.excerpt: Amazon has expanded Kindle Translate, its free AI-powered translation service for KDP indie authors, from two language pairs to six languages — English, Spanish, German, French, Italian and Portuguese. Authors can create, manage, price and publish fully formatted machine-translated editions of their books in a few clicks, with automatic accuracy checks before publication.
